question.text: Angel Funds (a sub-category of Cat I Venture Capital Funds) enjoy different investor-count treatment. What is the CORRECT position regarding investor limits in Angel Funds?

answer.text: Angel Funds are subject to the same 1,000 investor cap as other AIFs
Angel Funds are capped at 200 investors under the Companies Act
The 1,000 investor scheme cap does not apply in the same manner to Angel Funds (distinct angel investor regime)
Angel Funds have no minimum investor count

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 7/8 and AIF Regulations: Angel Funds operate under a distinct regime (separate regulation for angel investors), and the 1,000 investor per-scheme cap for regular AIF schemes does not apply in the same manner — the angel investor regulation governs Angel Funds separately. The Trap: Option A applies the general rule incorrectly. Option B conflates Companies Act. Option D is incorrect. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A focuses on Angel Fund specifics; XIX-C tests the contrast with the general AIF rule. Manager's Pro-Tip: When advising a sponsor debating Angel Fund registration, weigh the angel-investor-count relief against the restricted investee-company universe (start-ups) — Angel Funds cannot hold any investee indefinitely.
